title: Synthetic Dataset Mixer and Runner Compatibility Layer for Profile Generation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a synthetic dataset mixer and a runner compatibility layer that standardizes runner outputs for the benchmark harness to produce stable performance profiles for model onboarding and version pinning. This reduces variance from dataset sampling and runner differences and enables deterministic profile publishing across environments.
acceptance_criteria: Mixer integrates with existing dataset registry and can generate weighted mixes from 3+ datasets with reproducible seeds
Runner shim translates runner-specific output fields to harness canonical schema and preserves timing/latency metadata
Profiles generated using mixer+shim match existing profile format and include per-scenario sample counts and variance stats
End-to-end pipeline can pin model versions and publish profiles to catalog with artifact links
Automated tests cover mixer sampling distributions and shim translations; CI gate added
design_decisions: Use deterministic PRNG seed based on run_id + profile_version to ensure reproducibility
Mixer exposes sampling weights and stratification by prompt-length and scenario-type to mirror production traffic
Shim will be implemented as a light adapter layer instead of modifying runners to minimize disruption
Telemetry will include per-run percentiles, token-level timing, and KV-cache hit rate to aid performance tuning
tradeoffs: Adapter shim adds small latency in harness runs but avoids invasive runner changes
Synthetic mixing may not perfectly mimic customer distributions; provide tooling to import customer slices
Deterministic seeding reduces stochasticity but may mask rare nondeterministic issues; keep optional stochastic mode
plan: Week 1: prototype mixer with two datasets and deterministic seed support, design shim API
Week 2: implement shim adapters for 3 primary runner types and unit tests, add schema validation
Week 3: integrate with profile publisher, add telemetry hooks and dashboard
Week 4: run onboarding experiments for 5 recent models, iterate on weighting heuristics, prepare PRD and docs
risks: Mis-aligned schema expectations between runners causing silent data loss
Overfitting mixer weights to benchmark corpora leading to biased profiles
Performance overhead in CI causing test flakiness
testing_strategy: Deterministic A/B runs comparing baseline harness vs mixer+shim over 1000 sample seeds
Synthetic adversarial prompts to validate edge-case runner behavior
Regression tests using previously published profiles to ensure numeric stability
metrics: Profile variance reduction (stddev) target: 20% lower across scenarios
Runner translation error rate: <0.5% mismatched fields
End-to-end latency overhead: <2% relative to baseline harness
